svg.title: CONSISTENT HASHING: sketchnote
svg.text: CONSISTENT HASHING
Add or remove a node and move only a small share of the keys.
Core concept
THE PICTURE
Node A
Node B
Node C
Node D
key
Node E (new)
clockwise
only B→E range moves
HOW IT WORKS
Nodes and keys hash onto a ring.
A key belongs to the next node clockwise.
Adding a node moves only the keys in one arc
(~1/N), unlike hash % N which moves almost
everything. Virtual nodes even out the load.
Distributed caches, Cassandra, DynamoDB, L7
routing of video/doc IDs to servers.
CHECKLIST
Place nodes and keys on the same hash ring.
A key belongs to the first node clockwise
from it.
Use virtual nodes (many points per server) to
even out load.
Adding a node moves roughly 1/N of keys;
hash % N moves almost all of them.
SAY THIS
"Cache nodes sit on a consistent-hash ring with
virtual nodes, so adding a node remaps about 1/N
of keys instead of emptying the whole cache."
